source.title: Weights Read and Write Features: Scalable Parameter Decomposition Grounded in Activation Space
source.authors: T. M. Cao; Lisiane Pruinelli; My T. Thai

record.tranche_reason: The study uses ASPD, a different parameter-decomposition approach, to identify and intervene on components associated with IOI head roles in GPT-2 small.
record.gate_note: The IOI analysis uses the canonical prompt and reports component-level ablations, probe results, and cross-head interactions. It does not report a full-circuit ablation measuring IOI task performance or evaluate the original faithfulness, completeness, and minimality criteria. Results cited from Wang et al. are not recorded as this study's results.
record.test_reason: The study does not test the IOI circuit; it uses it as a showcase for its ASPD weight decomposition. It starts from Wang et al.'s head-level blueprint and picks heads from it ('We started with the blueprint of the IOI circuit'). It then decomposes those heads' weights into components on the single canonical prompt. It reports which components rebuild each head's attention pattern and how components interact across heads. It never measures IOI performance (logit difference or accuracy) after any intervention, never tests faithfulness, completeness or minimality, and never recovers the circuit independently, since the heads are given. The results check ASPD's interpretability on a known circuit, not whether any version holds.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that ASPD refines the known GPT-2 small IOI circuit into interpretable weight components and links mechanisms across heads. They acknowledge overly broad components (no 'token after John' or Mary-specific component) and components they only partly understand, and say they did not examine the ABC prompt. The paraphrase should add that the analysis starts from Wang et al.'s head blueprint on a single prompt, so the heads are not rediscovered. This qualifies the claim of 'Without training on circuit labels'.
record.recipe_differences: ASPD decomposes weights into activation-grounded read-write components and evaluates selected component interactions and direct weight edits; it is not the original head-level circuit-finding and evaluation procedure.

fits_no_version.finding: Removing small sets of ASPD weight components from the Q and K matrices of the heads in Wang et al.'s blueprint largely suppresses or shifts their characteristic attention patterns on the canonical prompt. The heads covered are H4.11, H5.5, H3.0, H8.6, H9.6 and H11.10. The effects are qualitative, with no IOI performance effect reported.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Individual IOI head attention patterns in GPT-2 small are carried by a few sparse rank-1 weight components.

fits_no_version.finding: Interaction scores link components across heads in the same order as Wang et al.'s description. The H3.0 duplicate-name component 224O and the H5.5 induction component 228O feed the H8.6 value components. H8.6 output components feed the query components of H9.6 and H11.10. These are interaction rankings only, not causal effects on IOI.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The head-to-head composition paths of the IOI circuit appear as aligned write and read weight components.

fits_no_version.finding: On the single prompt, the name-mover H9.6 value and output components found are gender-based ('female, woman'; 'predict next token is a male name'). The authors found no Mary-specific component. This hints at a gender heuristic on this prompt, which would bear on V6 but is not tested across prompts.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: On the canonical prompt, name-mover heads partly use gender features rather than pure name copying.

record.problems: The IOI evidence is on one model and the canonical prompt; the study does not report full-circuit ablation effects on IOI performance or quantify faithfulness, completeness, or minimality. The IOI component-intervention and probe results have no reported uncertainty estimates, and several results are qualitative.
record.rows_left_out: Additional component descriptions and interaction rankings in Appendix G and Figures 7–19 are not separately rowed where they add no distinct intervention or probe outcome beyond the selected component-role and cross-head results recorded above. The authors' cited findings from Wang et al. are excluded.

untested.parts: All of it: the 26-head, 7-class circuit, its faithfulness, completeness and minimality, and its effect on IOI performance. Head roles are taken from Wang et al., not tested.
All of it: no ablation of name-mover heads and no test of backup heads.
All of it: the IOI analysis covers GPT-2 small only. The Gemma and Qwen experiments are unrelated to IOI.
All of it: ASPD is applied to heads pre-selected from the original circuit, so it does not recover a circuit independently. No comparison of methods, ablation types or metrics.
All of it: no sweep over ablation type, metric or prompt distribution, and no fraction of behaviour explained.
All of it: only the canonical prompt 'When Mary and John went to the store, John gave a drink to' is used. The ABC prompt is explicitly not examined.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T2' and its V1/V4 supports labels are overturned. Every IOI result is a within-head attention pattern, a synthetic probe, or an interaction ranking internal to ASPD, on one prompt, with heads chosen from the original paper. Attribution patching on logit difference is used only to rank components; no values are reported. No uncertainty is given for any IOI result.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test the full 26-head, 7-class circuit as a whole, measure IOI performance after removing everything outside it, or evaluate the original faithfulness, completeness, and minimality criteria.
No ablation of main name-mover heads followed by a test for backup-head self-repair is reported.
The IOI circuit analysis is on GPT-2 small only. Other models are used for parameter-decomposition experiments, not for testing IOI circuits or component reuse across tasks.
The study applies ASPD to IOI, but does not systematically compare circuit-finding methods, ablation types, or evaluation metrics for equivalence of the recovered circuit.
No IOI sensitivity sweep over ablation type, metric, or prompt distribution, and no estimate of the fraction of behavior explained, is reported.
The IOI analysis uses the canonical prompt; it does not test other name orders, templates, ABC prompts, or prompts with more names.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small
rows.operation_detail: Removed dense QK components 12 and 70 from H4.11.

conditions.value: When Mary and John went to the store, John gave a drink to

rows.value: Attention patterns changed significantly, suppressing attention to previous tokens at many positions.
rows.note: The text describes dense-component edits as a group; it does not give a numeric effect.
rows.check: Measures how removing ASPD components changes H4.11's own attention pattern on one prompt. This shows the components rebuild the head's pattern, not that the head or circuit carries IOI. There is no IOI-performance measure, and the heads were chosen from the original blueprint, so it is not an independent recovery (V4).

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Selected IOI components and roles in GPT-2 small on the canonical prompt
reader_labels.reason: Component removals alter the described attention patterns and the probes/interactions associate components with duplicate-token, induction, S-inhibition, and name-mover computations; see R1–R14.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: ASPD applied to selected IOI mechanisms in GPT-2 small
reader_labels.reason: This different method identifies components with established IOI roles and reports matching effects under component ablation and probes; see R1–R14.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Component-level recovery of IOI mechanisms in the tested prompt
reader_labels.reason: The authors state that some mechanisms remain broad or incompletely understood, and that finer decomposition may be needed; this is not a demonstration of equivalence to the full circuit. See R3, R8, and R9.
